entities.summary: Gan De, also known as the Lord Gan, was an ancient Chinese astronomer and astrologer born in the State of Qi. Along with Shi Shen, he is believed to be the first in history known by name to compile a star catalogue, preceded by the anonymous authors of the early Babylonian star catalogues and followed by the Greek Hipparchus who is the first known in the Western tradition of Hellenistic astronomy to have compiled a star catalogue. He also made observations of the planets, particularly Jupiter. His writings are lost, but some of his works' titles and fragments quoted from them are known from later texts.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Gan De's compilation of a star catalogue marked an important milestone in ancient Chinese astronomy and astrology, contributing to the development of later astronomical knowledge. His work on planetary observations, particularly Jupiter, demonstrates his significant contributions to the field.
